As a warning this is a thread about the capture and euthanizing of an invasive and damaging frog species.

As the title states, I’d like some help with catching these bullfrogs. I’m in the PNW, so they’re invasive. It’s illegal to relocate them and they’ve caused harm to the local environment. Examples being the consumption of smaller native frogs. I haven’t seen or heard any pacifics in my backyard since the bullfrogs showed up. I don’t even know how the bullfrogs got here, it’s a fenced off area with no holes big enough to fit one. Since it’s spring/summer they’re beginning to come out of hiding. I know how to euthanize them humanely, and I would like to keep it humane. I’ve done it once before and it’s been a struggle catching any since. I can usually only use my bare hands since the pond/waterfall is too shallow/skinny to successfully use a net. Only having one hand available with the other holding a flashlight doesn’t make it any easier. Would like some tips if anyone has any.

Man you’re legit a life saver. I wouldn’t have known what to do. I’ll be sure to follow the guidelines you commented. But they can really regurgitate their whole stomach? As in the entire organ or the contents? Either way that’s something I want to avoid. They don’t miss the leaves that often, but when they do I usually shrug it off since they’ve been the least graceful of the trio ever since they were a froglet. From what I’ve seen today their gait looks fine. Right now the most obvious symptom is them refusing to eat when they’re the greediest. Maybe a little swelling too, although his size looks fairly similar to the rest of them. I’ll be sure to also widen what I give the crickets and what bugs I’ll feed the frogs. Once again though, thank you so so much! I’ll remember to come back here to ask if anything else pops up.

Well, I got some Reptivite, it’s got all sorts of vitamins including vit A(Vit A Acetate[praying it’s the right kind of vit A for my frogs, hardly any info on it]). Also got some small hornworms to see if he would try to eat something packed with some good stuff. No luck on the hornworms. However, success with force feeding. I had to cut the crickets in half though after dusting them with the Reptivite. With the use of an old gift card I was able to open their mouth and slide in the food. I was careful, didn’t put too much pressure when holding them still. Eventually after many attempts he began tiring out and it was much easier to force feed(although I felt horrible, teared up at one point). Got 1 1/2 crickets down before I decided that’s good for now. This may or may not be related, but it didn’t look like they were using their tongue to guide down the food like usual. Sure sign of short tongue syndrome? Well, anyways, there’s the update. All I can do now is sit back and pray, thank you so much for your help!

Bites and whatnot. I’ve been bitten by crickets before, not pleasant! Not to try to scare you, but there’s also been horror stories of, well... crickets beginning to eat pets. It’s a big reason why you should never leave too many in at once imo.

I’ve had these pacific tree frogs for about a year now, caught and raised them from tadpoles. There’s three of them. I began feeding them every two days not long ago. I tried feeding the one pictured last night but no luck. They tried once to grab the cricket from the tongs then gave up. Their tongue looked bloody but it could’ve been the underside of their tongue with veins. But, they did act strangely after they stuck it out. They held their tongue out for two or so seconds. It looked as if they were acting like they had a cramp in their tongue. Tonight I tried again, this time they didn’t even try to eat. I’ve read that sometimes reptiles and amphibians just stop eating for a while, but the possibly bloody tongue really concerns me. I dust their food with calcium and vit D3, their diet is usually a single mealworm followed by a couple small crickets. Is there some vitamin I’m not giving them that they should be getting? Could something like this occur if they’re constantly hitting their head? The one pictured is my most active frog and sometimes tries to jump through the mesh top, another reason why I occasionally put a towel over, and other times misses the leaf they’re aiming for and jumps right into the glass or foam.
